Definition: to shake (as in the wind), i.e. to quake; figuratively, to be loose morally, worthless or prodigal
BiblicalUsage: zâlal means to shake (as in the wind), that is to quake. In Deuteronomy 21:20 we read, "And they shall say unto the elders of his city, This our son is stubborn and rebellious, he will not obey our voice..." It appears again in Proverbs 23:20: "Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:".
TheologicalSignificance: zalal is to shake (as in the wind), that is to quake, and I hold that even a word used only a few times carries weight where God placed it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
